title: Stakeholder Signoff Compact + KPI Burnsheet
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, stakeholder-facing compact that pairs the minimum signoff matrix with the operational KPI burnsheet for upcoming feature launches. The intent is to reduce friction during final go/no-go while exposing the small set of metrics we will watch continuously for the first 72 hours.

Scope:
- Applies to feature launches that go into public traffic (beta -> general availability).
- Works as the single-source check for product/product-ops/eng/SRE signoff prior to ramp.
- Intended for fast updates (daily morning snapshot) and for the on-call rotation during day-0 to day-3.

How to use this document:
1) Product owner fills in the "acceptance window" values and owner names before go/no-go.
2) Eng/SRE/Support provide readiness flags in the signoff matrix (green/amber/red).
3) During ramp, the KPI burnsheet is updated in-place; deviations trigger the contingency table and the relevant owner is paged.

KPI Burnsheet (first 72h primary signals):
(Use this compact table to do quick triage; numbers are per-minute or percent depending on metric)

KPI | Target | Pre-roll (last 24h) | Current (rolling 15m) | Owner | Action if exceeds 
----|--------|--------------------|----------------------|-------|--------------------
Errors (5xx rate) | <0.5% | 0.2% | 0.8% | Eng-SRE (Liam) | Failover to fallback model + rollback flag
Median latency (p50 gen) | <120ms | 95ms | 135ms | Serving Runtime (Priya) | Scale up pool, enable smaller batch size
P95 latency (gen) | <600ms | 410ms | 720ms | Eng-Perf (Jordan) | Throttle non-critical routes, enable cache prefixing
API throughput (req/s) | baseline+20% | 420 | 510 | Product (Ava) | Open burst capacity, re-route low-pri tenants
Token cost per 1k output | < $1.20 | $0.95 | $1.35 | Finance/Optimize (Maya) | Apply suggested quantization profile for tail users
Quality regression (eval set delta) | < -0.5 BLEU-equivalent | -0.1 | -0.9 | Applied ML (Priya) | Rollback to prior model variant
User-facing error reports | 0 | 0 | 3 | Support Lead (TBD) | Triage and escalate to Eng-SRE
Adoption funnel drop | < 10% | +2% | -15% | Product Analytics (Ava) | Pause ramp; holdback cohort analysis

Note: "Current" is auto-updated by the daily snapshot script (see linked artifacts). If you see any red cell, update the "Incident runbook" section and ping the on-call.

Signoff Compact (pre-go):
Each row gets a green/amber/red. Product owner must obtain explicit green for the first three entries (readiness, security, SRE).

Role | Required signoff | Name | Flag (G/A/R) | Quick notes
-----|------------------|------|------------|--------
Product | Acceptance of UX degradation risk & rollout % | Jordan Kim | G | Feature gating plan in place
Eng (Serving) | Performance & fallback validated | Priya Shah | G | Canary benches completed
SRE | Capacity and SLO readiness | Liam O'Connor | A | Need one more region for redundancy
Security | Dataflow review & keys | Maya Rodriguez | G | KMS rotation confirmed
Support | Playbook & templates ready | Ava Patel | G | Escalation tree updated
Legal/Compliance | if regulated (optional) | Nora Lee | G | Data residency ok
Finance | Cost guardrails verified | Daniel Wu | G | Budget alert set

Contingency triggers (automatic + manual):
- Auto triggers: 5xx rate >1% sustained for 3m; P95 > 1500ms for 5m; Token cost spike > 25% vs baseline for 10m.
- Manual triggers: major UX regression reported by product research sample >10% (adoption funnel), legal escalations, or security incidents.

Immediate actions mapped to triggers:
- 5xx spike -> Eng-SRE initiate rollback to prior model variant; switch traffic to canary region; open incident channel #prod-incident and notify exec oncall.
- Latency spike -> Reduce batch size; add horizontal capacity; enable KV cache bypass for cold prefixes; set routing policy to low-latency tier.
- Cost spike -> Apply optimize suggested quant profile for non-prem customers; throttle background embeddings; enable cheaper routing pool.

Preflight Checklist (top items, required before flipping traffic):
- [ ] Canary pass: latency and error targets met for 4 consecutive hours
- [ ] Load test simulation at 2x expected peak (infra team signoff)
- [ ] Rollout %, breakpoint schedule & automatic holdbacks configured
- [ ] Support playbook + canned responses uploaded to Zendesk and Intercom
- [ ] Circuit-breaker + retry budgets verified in client SDKs
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards pinned & anomaly alerts configured
- [ ] Audit of data streams and KMS keys completed
- [ ] SLO runbook in confluence linked in incident channel
- [ ] Cost alerting and daily cost digest enabled for feature tags
- [ ] Legal checklist (if required) completed and signed
- [ ] Communications: status page template & customer comm draft ready
- [ ] Stakeholder sync scheduled for T+0, T+6h, T+24h

Incident runbook (short):
1) Triage on #prod-incident; set severity level.
2) Lead engineer attaches rolling 15m logs and pprof traces to incident thread.
3) If model quality regression -> swap model variant (prior model id) via model-router API (runbooks/exec command snippet in Confluence).
4) If latency/errors -> run emergency autoscale; re-route to fallback pool; notify customer success owners.
5) Postmortem owner assigned within 48 hours of severity incident.

Open questions / known risks:
- Multi-region cold start for private deployments still under test; regional SLOs may vary. (linked: GH PR #2345)
- Cost attribution for mixed-tenant runs needs a clearer tagging strategy (Finance to own).
- Non-deterministic eval flakiness on small eval sets — we should expand N and include synthetic adversarial prompts.

Meet cadence & artifacts:
- Daily morning snapshot (08:30 PT) during ramp: product-ops posts the KPI burnsheet to #launch-updates with a 1-paragraph readout.
- T+0 (launch) stakeholder call for first signal check (15m).
- T+6h operational sync (15m) if any amber/red signals.
- Post-launch review within 5 business days covering quality, latency, cost, adoption.

Next steps (owner mapped):
- Jordan: finalize acceptance window values and confirm ramp % schedule.
- Priya: validate canary performance with smaller batch size and QC test matrix.
- Liam: confirm cross-region failover and SRE on-call roster.
- Ava: publish support playbook and customer messaging.

Notes to self (short):
- Keep this compact — long playbooks live in Confluence. This doc is the canonical "what we watch and who hits the button".
- If you copy this, rename to include product slug and date.
